completedSteps.name: Task 9.1 - Implement src/tools/code_analysis.py (6 tools)
completedSteps.notes: 1425 lines. register(mcp, data) registers 6 tools on the FastMCP instance. Input schemas match the Node.js CodeAnalysisTools.js registerWith() block exactly (verified via two separate assertions — one in tests/unit/test_code_analysis_tools.py, a second in tests/parity/test_code_analysis_parity.py): analyze_code_structure(file_path: str, include_dependencies: bool=True, depth: int=2, token_budget: int=4000); find_dependencies(target: str, direction: Literal['upstream','downstream','both']='both', max_depth: int=3, token_budget: int=4000); trace_execution_path(function_name: str, file_path: str|None=None, max_depth: int=3, include_callers: bool=False, include_weights: bool=True, token_budget: int=4000); find_callers_callees(function_name: str, file_path: str|None=None, include_source: bool=False, token_budget: int=4000, cross_language: bool=False); trace_full_execution_chain(start: str, direction: Literal['forward','reverse','both']='forward', max_depth: int=5, languages: list[Literal['shell','fortran','python']]|None=None); find_env_dependencies(variable_name: str, show_exports: bool=True, limit: int=50, token_budget: int=4000). All tools return markdown text matching the Node.js TextContent shape. Delegates to data.graph_db via the GraphDBProtocol.query() surface — backend-agnostic, so Neptune today and anything the protocol accepts tomorrow. Uses the B3 GGSRTraversal.budget_aware_neighborhood for the token-aware weighted-context section via a shared _render_ggsr_section helper. cross_language=True routes the GGSR scoring through BRIDGE_DECAY_OVERRIDE (0.8) on EXECUTES/INVOKES hops; other relationship types keep the default HOP_DECAY (0.5). The cross-language cypher expands the SOURCES/INVOKES/EXECUTES/CALLS/USES/DEFINES edge set in a single variable-length path query (depth-clamped to 1..10). The languages filter on trace_full_execution_chain is applied after the graph walk so one DB round-trip serves any language subset. Degraded-mode boot (data=None) returns clear [ERROR] messages per tool rather than crashing. BRIDGE_DECAY_OVERRIDE re-exported from src/graphrag/__init__.py so the tool module can import it alongside GGSRTraversal. No modifications to mcp_server_node/.

completedSteps.name: Task 9.3 - Unit tests in tests/unit/test_code_analysis_tools.py
completedSteps.notes: 1179 lines, 54 tests. Schema parity assertions (parameter names, required flags, defaults, enum values for every tool); degraded-mode error-message shape parametrized across all 6 tools; empty-argument validation parametrized across all 6 tools; per-tool happy-path rendering against MockUnifiedDataAccess with add_response-seeded fragment matches; token_budget=0 suppresses the GGSR section; negative token_budget is silently clamped to zero; direct assertions on _apply_bridge_decay covering EXECUTES/INVOKES re-scoring via BRIDGE_DECAY_OVERRIDE (and confirming regular CALLS edges are untouched); languages filter on trace_full_execution_chain drops non-matching nodes while preserving matching ones; max_depth bounds — trace_execution_path clamped to 5, trace_full_execution_chain clamped to 10 (verified by inspecting the cypher string captured via a recording wrapper on graph_db.query); limit clamping on find_env_dependencies including the Node.js-parity note that limit=0 falls back to default 50 because `parseInt(limit, 10) || 50` treats 0 as falsy (initial test wrongly expected clamp to 1 — fixed in this phase to match Node.js behavior; negative values DO clamp to 1, upper-bound 99999 clamps to 500); graph-error propagation (raise_on_query → [ERROR] output); _label_to_language / _clamp helper tests.

completedSteps.name: Task 9.2 - Parity tests in tests/parity/test_code_analysis_parity.py
completedSteps.notes: 967 lines, 38 test nodes. Layout: 8 hermetic tests (test_framework_wires_against_mock_callers, test_framework_detects_sequence_divergence, test_bulleted_path_extractor_accepts_bold_variant, test_caller_callee_union_splits_on_section_headings, test_chain_node_extractor_ignores_statistics_section, test_section_entry_counter_respects_section_boundary, test_catalogue_has_minimum_coverage, test_schema_parity_with_nodejs_source — all always-runs) + 30 live-parity parametrized cases (5 per tool × 6 tools) gated on RUN_PARITY=1. pytest.mark.parity applied to module. AgentCoreToolCaller imported directly from tests/parity/test_semantic_search_parity to avoid duplicating the SSE/boto3 transport. Per-tool projections: analyze_code_structure uses _extract_markdown_headings SET_EQUALITY (shape of sections is the stable key) plus _extract_dependencies_entry_count TOLERANCE ±10% (Dependencies-section bullet count, Node.js returns this from Neo4j and Python from Neptune so small drift is expected); find_dependencies uses _extract_bulleted_paths SET_EQUALITY (order-insensitive because the two graph backends have different result-ordering semantics); trace_execution_path uses _extract_function_sequence EXACT (call order IS the parity key); find_callers_callees uses _extract_caller_callee_union SET_EQUALITY (union of Callers + Callees sections, parsing stops at next ## heading so Complexity Analysis doesn't leak); trace_full_execution_chain uses _extract_chain_node_names SET_EQUALITY reading only Direction subsections (not the Statistics block); find_env_dependencies uses _extract_script_paths SET_EQUALITY on the DEPENDS_ON_ENV list. Live-test env vars: RUN_PARITY=1 (required), NODEJS_RUNTIME_ID (ARN of mdc_mcp_rag_server-TMXDllG2Wi), PYTHON_RUNTIME_ID (ARN of mdc_mcp_rag_server_python-v5K2F8BGrN), AWS_REGION (default us-east-1). Default pytest run (no env var) reports 8 passed + 30 skipped, consistent with the hermetic-by-default contract from B4/B5.

followUps: Operator must rebuild the Docker image (python-code-analysis-v1 tag, per the rebuild instructions in .kiro/steering/06-python-port-progress.md), push to ECR, and update the AgentCore Runtime mdc_mcp_rag_server_python-v5K2F8BGrN to validate the 6 new tools against live Neptune. The Python staging runtime needs the same VPC/IAM connectivity as the production Node.js runtime (already in place since B11 smoke test); no new IAM permissions required.

Once the Python staging runtime is redeployed with code_analysis, run the live parity tests: RUN_PARITY=1 AWS_REGION=us-east-1 NODEJS_RUNTIME_ID=arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:903050880929:runtime/mdc_mcp_rag_server-TMXDllG2Wi PYTHON_RUNTIME_ID=arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:903050880929:runtime/mdc_mcp_rag_server_python-v5K2F8BGrN pytest mcp_server_python/tests/parity/test_code_analysis_parity.py -v. Expected: 30 live-parity cases PASS; any divergences are surfaced as individual pytest failures with ParityResult.describe() output. Cross-language cases (find_callers_callees with cross_language=true, trace_full_execution_chain) will give the first real validation of the GGSR BRIDGE_DECAY_OVERRIDE path against live data.

The Python port's cross-language cypher (MATCH p = (start)-[:SOURCES|INVOKES|EXECUTES|CALLS|USES|DEFINES*1..N]->(n)) is a simpler formulation than Node.js's traceCrossLanguageChain helper. If live-parity reveals divergences on trace_full_execution_chain, the fix is likely in how we assign 'language' to each returned node — the current label-substring mapping (Python|Fortran|Shell|Rocoto|Job prefixes) may need augmentation to match the Node.js helper's explicit label lists.

Task 10 (Phase B7: GraphRAGTools) is next in linear order. It will reuse the parity framework and the GGSRTraversal/GraphGuidedRetrieval pipeline the same way B6 did. B7 tools (get_code_context, get_change_impact, trace_data_flow, mark_as_modified, get_session_context, checkpoint_state, restore_checkpoint, etc.) exercise higher-level graph semantics and the SessionManager from B3.

find_callers_callees with include_source=true is accepted by the schema but the Python port does not (yet) inline source snippets. Node.js reads from vector_db to attach a snippet; implementing this cleanly requires the vector_db fan-out pattern from semantic_search.py — defer to a B7 or B8 polish pass.
